title: Enterprise stretch offers & SLA negotiation - cheatsheet and QBR scripts
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
This is a working cheatsheet for mid-market -> enterprise CSMs to use during QBRs and renewal cycles when testing stretch offers: Dedicated capacity upgrades, migration to Private, and premium SLA add-ons. The doc skims the commercial & technical signals, scripts for customer conversations, pricing/pack bundling patterns, risk mitigations, and internal escalation checklist.

Status / how to use this doc:
- Drafted for FY26 Q4 pilot (CS regional pilots).
- Use as a quick reference during QBR prep and renewal play planning.
- Add case-specific notes under the "Notes" section before meetings.
- Action owners: CSM + Solutions Engineer (pre-call), AE for commercial concessions, Solutions Eng + Infra for POA on Private.

Goals & success criteria (what counts as a win):
- Convert at least 20% of eligible mid-market renewals to a Dedicated upsell or Dedicated+SLA bundle in pilot cohort.
- Reduce in-contract customer-generated incidents by 40% for those who adopt premium SLA.
- Multi-month ARR uplift target per account: $25k+ avg for Dedicated, $60k+ for Private migrations.

Signals a customer is primed for a stretch offer (technical + commercial):
- Sustained growth: 30%+ month-over-month token consumption growth or 3x baseline over last 90 days.
- Tail latency pressure: median p95 inference latency approaching current SLA threshold or repeated queueing/burst throttles.
- KV cache misses & high repetition: high cost per effective token (we see repetitive prompt patterns causing wasted GPU time).
- Business triggers: upcoming product launch, new feature roadmap that requires predictable throughput, security/regulatory audit requests referencing data locality or isolation.
- Support signals: frequent severity-2 incidents or recurring performance regressions tied to shared-hosting variability.

Quick quant thresholds (CS shortcut) — pull from Metrics dashboard prior to outreach:
- Avg tokens/day > 50M OR concurrent sessions > 120 -> consider Dedicated sizing conversation.
- Spike events: 5+ >2x bursts/week -> consider burst capacity + SLA.
- Error rate > 0.8% or tail-latency (99th) > 2.5x median -> escalate to infra + propose premium SLA + routing guarantees.

Draft QBR slide agenda (10–15 mins focused upsell section):
1) Topline business outcomes driven by LLM usage (customer-provided KPIs).
2) Usage growth + cost/latency pain (metrics snapshot).
3) Proposed path options (Starter Dedicated, Dedicated+SLA, Private): bullets, high-level cost delta, expected improvements.
4) Migration plan & timeline (30/60/90 day milestones).
5) Ask & next steps (commitment window + kickoff owner).

Conversation scripts — tactical language for CSMs (pick and adapt):
- Opening (data-led): "We’ve seen steady growth in requests tied to X feature — your daily token count is up 3x. That’s great, but it means the shared-host queue is starting to impact p95 latency on peak days. We have two short-term ways to remove that variability: reserved Dedicated capacity, or a Private deployment if you need network isolation."
- If they push on price: "Totally fair — here’s how the economics look: switching to Dedicated reduces your per-token bill by roughly Y% and cuts tail latency risk. Combine that with a premium SLA and we’ll commit to xms p95 and 99.9% availability during business hours. We can run a 30-day pilot to prove impact before committing long-term."
- Objection: "We can’t sign a long contract now." -> "We hear that — propose a stepped approach: 3-month reserved with optional extension, or a pilot credit-backed migration. We’ll instrument key SLOs and share a joint dashboard; if you don’t see the promised wins we’ll work a split refund/exit."

Commercial bundle patterns (pricing flavors to present quickly):
- Capacity-first bundle: Reserved GPU pool sizing + baseline throughput SLA. Pricing = baseline monthly + overage at pre-agreed rate. Good for predictable high-throughput customers.
- SLA-lite bundle: Small reserved slice + premium SLA for latency/uptime during business hours. Lower commitment than full Dedicated.
- Private migration bundle: Migration services + Private control plane + 12-mo commitment with escalation credits. Include optional onboarding days and security review support.
- Add-ons: priority support, faster incident response SLA, dedicated TAM, extended observability retention.

Technical prep checklist for Solutions Eng (pre-QBR):
- Export last 90d usage from platform (tokens/day, peak concurrency, p95/p99 latency).
- Collect recent incident log lines + stack traces (if any).
- Confirm data residency / compliance notes (does customer require VPC/HSM?).
- Estimate Dedicated sizing using usage percentiles (50/90/99).
- Draft short migration runbook: expected downtime, rollout steps, test plan, rollback.

Risk & mitigation table (CS shorthand):
- Risk: Customer worries about lock-in -> Mitigation: Step approach, pilot, rollback window, exportable cache and model-variants.
- Risk: Cost concerns -> Mitigation: Provide forecast model, show per-token regressions, offer pilot discount.
- Risk: Security/compliance hurdles -> Mitigation: Engage security pre-sales, share private-deploy compliance checklist, schedule KMS/HSM architecture review.

Internal escalation path (who to loop in):
- Pre-sale pricing exceptions -> AE + Pricing desk (contact: Marcus Patel).
- Sizing or infra risk -> Solutions Eng (Priya Nair) + Serving Runtime lead.
- Private/on-prem requests -> Platform Eng + Security (start with security intake ticket: JIRA:CS-4821).

Sample email templates (pick and edit)
- Short: "Hey <Name>, following up from today’s QBR — based on your growth curve we recommend we discuss a small Dedicated trial to stabilize peak latency. Can we lock 30 minutes next week to review sizing and costs?"
- Longer (commercial + technical):"Hi <Name>, thanks again for the session. Attached is a one-pager showing three options tuned to your usage: 1) Reserved Dedicated (stabilize latencies), 2) Dedicated+SLA (guaranteed p95/uptime), 3) Private (isolation & compliance). We recommend a 30-day trial of option 1 or 2 — we’ll instrument SLOs and report back. Next steps: confirm preferred option by <date> and we’ll schedule kickoff."

Negotiation concessions playbook (triage):
- Always start with value (predictable latency, lower cost per token, faster incident response).
- Use a fixed pilot credit instead of blanket discount if they’re price-sensitive.
- If they push on term length, prefer a shorter reserved term with higher per-unit than a long low-term discount.
- Avoid broad permanent discounts at renewal — structure tied to performance metrics or adoption milestones.

Checklist for Private migration conversation (legal/security cues):
- Customer must confirm scope of data that needs to be isolated (PII / PHI / proprietary models).
- KMS/HSM requirements (vendor & BYOK vs Redwood managed).
- Audit window & logging retention requirements.
- Network architecture constraints (air-gapped? VPN only?).
- Timeline for security review (estimate 6–8 weeks depending on third-party audits).

Open questions / TODOs (items to resolve before wider roll-out):
- Define standard pilot success criteria (SLO thresholds + revenue delta) — need input from Product.
- Fill in standard 30/60/90 migration runbook template in Confluence (owner: Priya).
- Packaging: finalize price bands for Dedicated sizes (small/medium/large) + published uplift % for SLA (pricing desk).

Notes (place to paste account-specific snippets before call):
- [Paste tokens/day, recent incidents, customer quotes about latency or cost].

References and links:
- Confluence QBR template: confluence:CS/QBR-templates
- Internal pricing band doc: confluence:pricing/dedicated-bands (TBD)
- Pilot contract template: github.com/redwood-inference/contract-templates/pull/29

Versioning / history:
- 2025-09-22: initial draft (Elena)
- 2025-10-10: added negotiation scripts + pilot checklist (Marcus)
- 2025-11-05: added commercial bundle patterns and updated thresholds (Priya)

Bottom line (one-liner for quick read):
Use data-first QBR narratives (usage + pain) -> propose low-friction pilot (30–90 days) -> instrument SLOs -> convert to Dedicated/Private with clear migration SLAs and performance guarantees.

-- end of cheatsheet --
